metadata.title: Xiaomi shares jump over 8% as premium phone sales cushion rising chip costs

content.text:
Investing.com -- Xiaomi shares surged more than 8% on Wednesday after its smartphone business performed better than expected in the third quarter, suggesting the Chinese technology group is using higher-priced devices to offset rising memory chip costs.
The stock recorded its biggest daily gain in nearly three weeks after smartphone revenue remained broadly flat in the September quarter, outperforming analyst expectations for a 6% decline. The average selling price of Xiaomi devices climbed nearly 40% to a record, reflecting stronger sales of premium models.
The shift up-market is helping Xiaomi manage a shortage of conventional memory chips, as growing demand from artificial intelligence data centres puts pressure on semiconductor supplies and raises component costs for consumer electronics manufacturers.
The company's latest Xiaomi 18 Fold, launched towards the end of the third quarter, carries a price tag of more than 10,000 yuan ($1,500), positioning it against Apple's premium devices and competing offerings from Huawei.
Xiaomi's broader financial performance remained under pressure. Revenue fell 5.2% year on year to 107.2 billion yuan in the three months ended September, a smaller decline than analysts had anticipated. Net income dropped 68% to 3.9 billion yuan.
Its electric-vehicle and artificial-intelligence division recorded a loss of 3.4 billion yuan, with executives attributing the deficit to increased investment in AI during a post-results call.
Vehicle deliveries also weakened, falling 7% from a year earlier to 100,975 units. However, Xiaomi reaffirmed its plan to begin selling cars in Germany in the third quarter of 2027 as part of its wider European expansion.
President William Lu said during the earnings call that the company's preparations for the European market were progressing smoothly. Xiaomi has signed agreements with eight leading German dealerships, while companies in other European markets have also approached the group about potential cooperation.
The company is preparing vehicles for Germany, Sweden, Spain and Italy, with testing taking place across seven facilities. Lu said Xiaomi was also making progress in both left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive markets, although its initial expansion strategy prioritises left-hand-drive countries.
